question: Under separable stationary colored noise, does known-spectrum whitening in Fourier coordinates (a row/column scaling that keeps the matrix structure) let the same-sample 2SDR pipeline recover its white-noise behaviour, and can the corrected holdout score choose among fitted estimators on the original pixel scale without clean targets?

dataset.clean_role: the clean_observed stack (identical across SNR) generates the colored observations and scores reconstructions; it is never used for selection
dataset.noise_level: sigma2 = (base/s0) * kappa, kappa = tr(C^-1 Sigma_S)/tr(Sigma_S) with C the mean-one AR(1) spectrum and Sigma_S the ensemble-centred clean covariance: the colored condition has the same mean Mahalanobis signal energy as the white-noise reference at label s0. s0 in {.04,.05,.06} is reported as the white-reference SNR.

noise.model: separable periodic AR(1), mean-one spectrum per axis (fourier_2sdr.whitening.periodic_ar1_spectrum), marginal variance sigma2
noise.rho_rationale: 0.6 is the primary lag-one correlation; 0.3 and 0.8 are sensitivity checks; rho = 0 (flat spectrum, whitening is the identity) is the white-noise anchor
noise.noise_only_rationale: estimated-spectrum variant: independent signal-free images (one tenth of the particle count), the analogue of background regions or dark frames; separable rank-one spectrum estimate

selection.stage1: nested upper-envelope Tu SURE of experiments/seventy_s_same_sample (unchanged)
selection.whitened_tu_sigma2: 1 (the known spectrum including sigma2 divides out)
selection.unwhitened_tu_sigma2: marginal sigma2 (white-noise assumption, misspecified under colored noise)
selection.small_core_rule: if Stage I selects a 1x1 core, r <= m-1 forces r = 0
selection.split_pca_ranks_rationale: uniform step 5 up to the PCA search cap 100

part_b_split.candidates: for raw and whitened coordinates: one upper MPCA envelope (64x64) fitted on the fit split; every nested (p,q) in split_grid^2 gives a complete 2SDR estimator with r from HHI GIC on the fit-split core, plus the full-core MPCA estimator; vector PCA with HHI GIC rank; mean-only; vector PCA with r in split_pca_ranks scored by the same split score (pixel-risk-selected PCA)
part_b_split.grid_rationale: 64 is half of the 130-pixel axis; the grid is the multiples of 4 to 24 then of 8 to 64
part_b_split.score: corrected holdout score on the original pixel scale with known (or estimated) diagonal noise covariance; it scores the complete two-stage estimator
part_b_split.outputs: part_b_candidates.csv: split_sure, score_true_risk, test_true_risk per candidate

reported_design.rho_0.6: first 10 realizations per s0 (s0 = .04 and .05 from run formal_rho06, s0 = .06 from run formal_rho06_s006)
reported_design.estimated_spectrum_part_b: rho = 0.6, first 5 realizations per s0, Part B only; the separable spectrum estimated from the noise-only images replaces the known spectrum both for whitening and in the score covariance; same seeds as the known-spectrum runs, so the comparison is paired
reported_design.seed_rule: noise_base + 1000*round(10*rho) + 100*round(100*s0) + k; noise-only images use seed + 500000; the Part B split uses the same seed
